_doc: OBJECT > LOCK STOPS MATERIALIZING — transcripts/LAYER_STRUCTURE.md §13,
RULED by JYH 2026-07-28.
§13 repealed materialization and the LAYERS-PANEL path was repaired
(`Document::toggling_element_lock` / `Document.togglingElementLock`, gated
by lock_toggle_no_materialization.json). `Object > Lock` — the menu item,
Ctrl+2, and the `lock_selection` op verb — was NOT. It kept a second,
recursive implementation (`lock_element` in jas_dioxus, `lockRecursive` in
JasSwift) that stamped `locked = true` onto every descendant of a Group.
WHY THAT WAS WORSE THAN A LEFTOVER, and why it is fixed here rather than
recorded. §13.1 landed `jas:locked` SVG persistence the same day, so the
stamped flags SURVIVE SAVE AND RELOAD. Under inheritance they are also
INDIVIDUALLY UNREMOVABLE — opening the parent leaves every child locked
and there is no UI anywhere that clears a single one (`Unlock All` is the
whole document or nothing). `unlocking_a_group_frees_its_children` below
is that exact artist story, and it is the case the residue reddened.
THE RESIDUE IS GROUP-ONLY IN BOTH PORTS — measured, not assumed. Rust
recursed under `new.is_group()`, which is `matches!(self,
Element::Group(_))` and excludes `Element::Layer`; Swift recursed in its
`case .group` arm alone. So locking a LAYER never stamped in either port,
which is why `object_lock_on_a_layer_writes_only_the_layers_own_flag` is a
control here and not a headline. It is kept precisely so the repair cannot
be mistaken for 'stop writing the flag'.
NOT ONE GOLDEN IN THIS FAMILY WAS GENERATED FROM THE BEHAVIOUR IT PINS,
which is what let the red be measured in both ports before either moved
(the device is §15.5's). Two mechanisms:
* IDENTITY — the two headline cases point at
lock_toggle_group_locked_expected.json and
lock_toggle_leaf_locked_expected.json, goldens the panel family already
owns. That pins `Object > Lock` as an EQUATION: locking a group from
the Object menu must produce exactly what the Layers-panel lock button
produces on the same group. Two functions doing the same job
differently is how this diverged, so the gate says they are the same
job rather than describing the answer twice.
* EQUATION AGAINST A CONTROL — `unlocking_a_group_frees_its_children`
and `control_clicking_a_child_of_an_untouched_group` share one golden.
Lock a group and unlock it again, and a click on its child must land
exactly where a click lands when nothing ever happened.
The three genuinely new goldens were DERIVED from
lock_toggle_group_locked_expected.json by flipping named flags, not
produced by any runner.
WHAT THIS FAMILY CANNOT REACH. `lock_selection` reads `doc.selection` and
the op corpus can only seed that through `select_element` / `select_rect`,
so a selection holding an element AND its own ancestor — which production
can build through the Layers panel — is not expressible here. Also
untouched: `unlock_all`, whose post-state selection DIVERGES between the
ports today (jas_dioxus clears it, JasSwift re-selects every formerly
locked path) — a real defect, deliberately left to its own wave so this
family stays a gate on materialization alone.
name: lock_selection_setup_is_a_layer_holding_a_group_of_two_rects

_doc: THE HEADLINE. Object > Lock on a GROUP writes the group's own flag and NOTHING ELSE. Pinned BY FILE IDENTITY against the Layers-panel lock button's own golden: the two paths must be one behaviour. Before the repair both rects came back locked:true — flags the artist never set, which `jas:locked` then wrote into the saved file.
name: object_lock_on_a_group_writes_only_the_groups_own_flag

_doc: THE PROTECTION SURVIVES THE REPAIR. After the group is locked, a click on a child is still refused — by INHERITANCE now rather than by a stamped flag, and the SELECTION half of this case was already correct before the repair. It is nonetheless one of the three red cases, because the golden compares the whole document and the residue left its flags there; that is the honest reading, and the case still earns its place as the one that stops the repair from being 'lock less'.
name: a_child_of_a_group_locked_from_the_object_menu_is_not_selectable

_doc: THE ARTIST STORY THE RULING IS ABOUT. Lock a group from the Object menu, then unlock that group — and its children are free again, because nothing was ever written onto them. Pinned as an EQUATION against control_clicking_a_child_of_an_untouched_group below: the round trip must leave the document and the next click exactly where they started. Before the repair the children stayed locked:true with no UI able to clear them individually, so the click was refused and the selection came back empty.
name: unlocking_a_group_frees_its_children

_doc: THE CONTROL that gives the case above its meaning: a click on a group's child in a document nothing has touched. Behaviour this ruling does not speak to, which is why the shared golden could be derived without consulting the code under repair.
name: control_clicking_a_child_of_an_untouched_group

_doc: DEPTH CONTROL. Locking a LAYER leaves the group inside it and both grandchildren untouched. Green before and after — Rust's `is_group()` excludes Layer and Swift recursed only in its `case .group` arm — so this case pins that the repair is 'stop recursing', not 'stop writing the flag', and it watches the one depth the group cases cannot see.
name: object_lock_on_a_layer_writes_only_the_layers_own_flag

_doc: LEAF CONTROL, pinned BY FILE IDENTITY against the panel family's leaf golden. A leaf has no children to materialize onto, so this case is unchanged by the repair and holds the two paths to the same answer on the simplest input there is.
name: object_lock_on_a_leaf_flips_its_own_flag
